Background Matrix.Type: A uniform, textured substrate forming the base layer with a granular or speckled appearance and a consistent, non-organic pattern
Background Matrix.Color: Light gray with subtle tonal variations and slight mottling, appearing matte and evenly distributed across the entire visible area
Background Matrix.Size: Fills the entire visible area, extending from edge to edge of the frame and approximately square in shape, with no defined boundaries
Background Matrix.Material: A solid, non-reflective, possibly composite or ceramic-like material with a fine-grained, granular texture
Background Matrix.Composition: A homogeneous mixture with a fine, porous structure and embedded particulates, forming a consistent and uniform structure throughout
Background Matrix.Quantity: One continuous, singular matrix covering the entire field of view
Background Matrix.Relative Location: Occupies the entire visual field and serves as the base layer underlying all speckles
Background Matrix.Orientation: Flat, horizontal, and isotropic, uniformly aligned across the image with no discernible tilt or directional bias
Background Matrix.Connection or Attachments: Serves as the substrate for the speckles, with no visible attachment points or separations; forms a single, continuous surface

Speckles.Type: discrete, irregularly shaped particles distributed across the surface, varying in density and clustering
Speckles.Color: dark gray to black, with slight tonal variation indicating depth or surface texture differences, some appearing slightly more saturated or shadowed
Speckles.Size: ranging from 0.1 to 5 mm in diameter, with variable shapes and sizes including small dots (sub-millimeter), elongated clusters, and diffuse patches
Speckles.Material: solid, non-organic, dense, and opaque, with a matte or slightly rough texture
Speckles.Composition: composed of discrete, independent particles or aggregated material, possibly mineral or carbonaceous, embedded within the matrix with no visible chemical or structural bonding between them
Speckles.Quantity: numerous, covering the entire visible surface, with no discernible pattern or density gradient, estimated to be in the thousands
Speckles.Relative Location: scattered randomly across the entire background matrix, with no specific focal point or preferred region
Speckles.Orientation: randomly oriented, with no consistent directionality or alignment
Speckles.Connection or Attachments: each speckle is individually separated and independently embedded within the matrix, with no visible bonding, adhesion, or interconnection to other speckles
